content.text: should these tests succeed or fail? i'm finding it difficult to figure out if they should pass/fail and how to even debug theses things
PR -
https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/pull/1846
was this report to just take the @ignore's off the tests or to take them off and fix them so they work? just asking for any future bugs I might do
normally these tests should always pass. In some special cases where an
expected
Exception is specified then you want the system to fail, but the test still passes.
I just pulled off the
@Ignore
and ran the tests. They all passed which is nice and easy.
If the tests were still failing then the work is to figure out if the actual test is broken (ie. the interaction has changed) or if there is a problem in the codebase.
..i'm confused. I've been working on these for a few weeks. tried taking the @ignore statements off and they failed, so i've spent more than a week trying to get them working
You may have uncovered a bigger problem. It appears tests that should fail are not stopping the build or even showing up. More discussion on slack in the bleeding-edge channel.
After rebasing on `main`, these tests are failing again.
Alright
I'm ready to hand this ticket back into your waiting hands. I've got a bunch of other ones to fix.
<sarcasm>cool, its like christmas all over again</sarcasm>
If you want I'll take this one and you can take FCREPO-3230.
No, its a good learning experience. I just have a question:
In the tests, generally, it PUTs an item into the repository and then checks that it was added correctly. Some of the tests define the user and.or date used in the item.
What i'm seeing is the tests are failing due to Server Managed Property Execptions, which i guess is that the server doesnt like parts of the metadata being set?? how do I remedy that?
Thanks

That is the whole thing with "relaxed" mode. The server normally won't let you set a server managed triple (like createdBy or createdTime). But when the server is in "relaxed" mode it should allow that.
It is possible the test is not actually getting the server into "relaxed" mode at all.
Normally you'd just add
-Dfcrepo.properties.management=relaxed
to the JAVA_OPTS. You may need to ensure that is happening.
Hey

, how is this ticket going? I just realized that for this to actually work there is changes needed in the HttpRdfService and SparqlVisitor as they currently either remove server managed triples (if we provide a
Prefer: handling=lenient
header or throw an Exception.
Additional work is needed to check for the relaxed property and not remove the triples but also not throw an exception.
Hi, sorry, lots of things been going on, a lot of it not work related (did get a new laptop, so setting that up has been an experience)

I figured there was an issue as I got as far as putting the server in relaxed mode and....it still didn't work, even though the server really thought it was in relaxed mode. And trying to figure out where to look in the server seems to be beyond me right now
